name: teable
description: Teable AI Tools CLI for operating Teable projects, tables, fields, views, records, SQL read queries, and related app/automation workflows with a safe read-before-write process.

options.description: Enable debug output (verbose logging to stderr)
Show CLI version

help:
Usage: teable [options] [command]

Teable AI Tools CLI for operating Teable projects, tables, fields, views, records, SQL read queries,
and related app/automation workflows with a safe read-before-write process.

Options:
  -V, --version                  Show CLI version
  --debug                        Enable debug output (verbose logging to stderr)
  -h, --help                     display help for command

Setup:
  auth|init [options]            Manage auth for teable
  config                         Manage project-level CLI configuration
  link [options] [baseId]        Bind this directory to a project so commands here need no --base-id

Resources:
  query                          query operations (schema, execute, inline, explain,
                                 manifest-schema, validate, generate, lint, deps, coverage, repairs,
                                 repair-apply, repair-dismiss)
  operation                      operation operations (capabilities, preview)
  media                          media operations (generate, get, cancel)
  base                           project operations (create, get, list, update, delete)
  template                       template operations (search, install, status, submit, guide,
                                 guide-save)
  table                          table operations (create, get, update, delete)
  field                          field operations (create, get, update, delete)
  record                         record operations (create, get, update, delete)
  view                           view operations (create, get, update, delete)
  app                            app operations (list, get-code, create, update, delete, publish,
                                 status, unpublish, login-config, ai-docs, ai-enable, init, clone,
                                 pull, push, versions, rollback)
  automation                     automation operations (list, get, update, activate, setup-trigger,
                                 delete, test-node, delete-node, generate-script,
                                 generate-flowchart, get-script-input, get-runs, get-run)
  routine                        routine operations (create, list, get, update, activate,
                                 deactivate, delete, run-now, get-runs, get-run)
  authority                      authority operations (get, export, diff, apply, enable, disable,
                                 role-list, role-get, role-delete, role-duplicate)
  folder                         folder operations (create, update, delete, move)
  artifact                       artifact operations (list, create, update, get, share)
  scrape                         scrape operations (search, inspect, run, status)
  integration                    integration operations (connect, list, get-token, search)
  env                            env operations (list, set, update, delete)
  secret                         secret operations (list, set, grant, revoke, delete)
  sandbox                        sandbox operations (tool)
  skill                          skill operations (list, import-github, import-file, update)

Tools:
  get-node-tree [options]        Get the tree structure of all nodes (tables, automations, apps,
                                 etc.) in a project
  search-api [options]           Search available APIs by description to find the right endpoint
  get-doc [options]              Get documentation for a topic
  tools                          Tool discovery and metadata commands
  sql-query [options]            Execute SQL query on tables
  get-collaborators [options]    Get collaborators in the current project with pagination and search
  get-ai-config [options]        Get AI field configuration documentation with available models
  import [options]               Import tabular data into Teable (analyzes by default; --table-name
                                 creates, --table-id appends)
  import-airtable [options]      Import an Airtable base into Teable
  import-google-sheet [options]  Import a Google spreadsheet into Teable
  import-status [options]        Query import job status for a table
  upload-attachment [options]    Upload a local file as an attachment
  call-api [options]             Call any Teable API (axios-style: method, url, params, data)
  trigger-ai-fill [options]      Trigger AI generation for an AI-configured field
  send-email [options]           Send an email to one or more recipients (system SMTP by default, or
                                 --smtp for a custom transport)

Commands:
  help [command]                 display help for command

Project = API base (bse-prefixed ID). Commands use teable base and --base-id.

Examples:
  teable table get --table-id tblXXXX            List table metadata
  teable record get --table-id tblXXXX           Query records
  teable table create --name Tasks --fields '["Title:text","Status:sel:Todo,Done"]'

subcommands.name: ai-docs
subcommands.summary: How the app calls AI through Teable proxy (usage + available model keys)
subcommands.description:
Shortcut for: get-doc --topic app.ai

Returns documentation on how an app-builder app calls AI through Teable's
proxy, with the available model keys for the current project. Covers:
  - Injected env vars (TEABLE_AI_API_BASE_URL / TEABLE_AI_API_KEY)
  - Server-side usage with the OpenAI / Anthropic SDK
  - How to enable AI access if it is off
  - Available model keys (e.g. aiGateway@openai/gpt-5.5@teable)

options.description: Teable API server base URL; falls back to TEABLE_ENDPOINT env var, then saved config
Indent JSON for human readability
Personal access token; falls back to TEABLE_TOKEN env var
Target project ID (required, e.g. bseXXXX). Set default: `teable config base-id <id>`.

subcommands.name: ai-enable
subcommands.summary: Enable AI access for an app (provisions the AI proxy key)
subcommands.description:
Enable AI access for an app so it can call AI through Teable's proxy.
Provisions the proxy key and injects TEABLE_AI_API_BASE_URL /
TEABLE_AI_API_KEY on the next preview restart. Idempotent — safe to run
when already enabled. System-model usage consumes credits; BYOK models
run on the space's own key (no Teable credits).

The key value is never printed. Run `app ai-docs` for usage + models.

subcommands.name: clone
subcommands.summary: Clone an app repository locally for development with external tools
subcommands.description:
Clone an existing Teable app repository for local development with your own tools (not the in-app App Builder).

What it does:
  1. Clones the app repository into <dir> with the git remote named `teable` (an app that was never generated gets the scaffold as version 1 first).
  2. Writes AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .env and the table-schema context files (teable.md, schema/*.json).

Parameters:
  - appId (required): the app to clone
  - dir: target directory (default: ./<app-name>)

Unlike `teable app get-code` (a read-only snapshot), this checkout is meant to be edited and pushed back with `teable app push`.
Requires app editing permission (project Owner/Creator) and a deployment with a git registry.

options.description: App ID to clone (appXXXX), from `teable app list`
Directory to clone into (must be empty or absent). Defaults to a folder named after the app in the current directory.
Teable API server base URL; falls back to TEABLE_ENDPOINT env var, then saved config
Indent JSON for human readability
Personal access token; falls back to TEABLE_TOKEN env var
Target project ID (required, e.g. bseXXXX). Set default: `teable config base-id <id>`.

subcommands.name: create
subcommands.summary: Create or update an app with AI
subcommands.description:
Build or modify a web application with Teable integration.

Actions:
  create: Create a new app
  update: Modify an existing app

Parameters:
  action: create or update (required)
  name: App name (optional)
  prompt: App-building prompt for teable app create/update CLI (required)
  appId: App ID to update (required for update action)
  tableIds: Table IDs to include in app context (optional)
  attachmentTokens: Image tokens for UI reference (optional)
  sendMode: queue or steer, update action only (optional)

Busy app builder (update action):
  Default (queue): a busy app queues the prompt; it runs automatically when the current generation finishes.
  steer: redirect the in-flight generation with the prompt instead of waiting; use it to adjust work that is already running. Falls back to queue when nothing is running.

Important rules for prompt:
  First complete any requested setup, table inspection, analysis, or data changes.
  Do not pass setup, analysis, or data-seeding steps to App Builder.
  Include only the app purpose, UI/workflow, explicit constraints, relevant table IDs, and verified data context.
  Keep the user intent without adding extra features or details.
  Do not use markdown formatting in the prompt.
  Do not specify technology stack unless the user explicitly requests it.

Workflow:
  Use get-apps tool first to check existing apps.
  If a matching app exists, use update action.
  Otherwise, use create action.

subcommands.name: get-code
subcommands.summary: Download app source code as a local read-only context snapshot
subcommands.description:
Download the source code of an app into the local workspace for reading.

Use this when the user mentions an app (an `@app[name](id:appXXX)` marker) and you need its
implementation as context: understanding how it works, referencing or imitating it, or
coordinating changes across apps.

Parameters:
  - appId (required): The app ID (e.g. appXXXXXX)

Behavior:
  - Extracts the latest saved version into `~/.teable/refs/<appId>/`
  - The directory is a detached snapshot: edits do NOT change the app and may be
    overwritten by the next download. To modify the app, update it through the app builder.
  - Env files are excluded; app secrets are never included.

Requires app editing permission (project Owner/Creator) on the app's project.

options.description: App ID to download source code for (from an @app mention or get-apps)
Teable API server base URL; falls back to TEABLE_ENDPOINT env var, then saved config
Indent JSON for human readability
Personal access token; falls back to TEABLE_TOKEN env var
Target project ID (required, e.g. bseXXXX). Set default: `teable config base-id <id>`.

subcommands.name: init
subcommands.summary: Create an app and check out its repository locally for development with external tools
subcommands.description:
Create a new Teable app and check out its repository locally for development with your own tools (not the in-app App Builder).

What it does:
  1. Creates the app in the current project and writes the platform scaffold as version 1.
  2. Clones the app repository into <dir> with the git remote named `teable`.
  3. Writes AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .env and the table-schema context files (teable.md, schema/*.json).

Parameters:
  - name (required): app name
  - dir: target directory (default: ./<app-name>)
  - folderId: project folder for the app

Then: cd <dir>, read CLAUDE.md, `pnpm install && pnpm dev`, and use `teable app push` to save versions.
Requires app create permission (project Owner/Creator) and a deployment with a git registry.

Name of the new app

subcommands.name: login-config
subcommands.summary: Configure login/authentication for an app
subcommands.description:
Configure login/authentication for an app.

Use this tool to enable, update, or disable login for a generated app.
When enabled, end-users of the app must authenticate before accessing it.

Parameters:
  appId (required): The app ID
  loginConfig (required): Login configuration object, or null to disable. It replaces the whole config: to add a provider, resend the current config with the provider appended

loginConfig fields:
  enabled: true to enable login, false to disable
  userTableId: table ID that stores user records
  emailFieldId: field ID of the email column in the user table
  providers: array of login providers, each with a "type" field:
    - { "type": "email-otp" }: Email one-time password login
    - { "type": "google" }: Google OAuth login
    - { "type": "teable" }: Teable OAuth login
    - { "type": "oidc" }: SSO login through the identity provider the instance admin configured
  access (optional): access control configuration:
    - mode: "open" (anyone can sign up), "domain" (restrict to email domains), "existing-only" (only existing users)
    - domains: array of allowed email domains (only for "domain" mode)

Examples:
  Enable email OTP: { enabled: true, userTableId: "tblXXX", emailFieldId: "fldXXX", providers: [{ type: "email-otp" }] }
  Disable login: null

options.description: The ID of the app to configure login for
Teable API server base URL; falls back to TEABLE_ENDPOINT env var, then saved config
Login configuration object, or null to disable login entirely
Indent JSON for human readability
Personal access token; falls back to TEABLE_TOKEN env var
Target project ID (required, e.g. bseXXXX). Set default: `teable config base-id <id>`.

subcommands.name: push
subcommands.summary: Push a local app checkout to Teable and record it as a new app version
subcommands.description:
Save a local app checkout to Teable: commit (optional), pre-check, push to the app repository, and record the commit as a new app version. Teable then refreshes a running preview of the app and notes the change in the app chat.

Pre-checks that stop the push:
  - platform-owned (locked) files were modified — revert them, the platform rewrites them anyway
  - an env file or the CLI config (.teable/cli) is tracked, or a commit about to be pushed touches one — secrets never go into the repository, not even into its history
  - the app repository moved ahead of the checkout — run `teable app pull` first

Parameters:
  - message: commit subject for uncommitted changes; also the version description
  - dir: checkout directory (default: found from the current directory)

Publishing is separate: run `teable app publish --wait` only when the user asks.

subcommands.name: update
subcommands.summary: Create or update an app with AI
subcommands.description:
Build or modify a web application with Teable integration.

Actions:
  create: Create a new app
  update: Modify an existing app

Parameters:
  action: create or update (required)
  name: App name (optional)
  prompt: App-building prompt for teable app create/update CLI (required)
  appId: App ID to update (required for update action)
  tableIds: Table IDs to include in app context (optional)
  attachmentTokens: Image tokens for UI reference (optional)
  sendMode: queue or steer, update action only (optional)

Busy app builder (update action):
  Default (queue): a busy app queues the prompt; it runs automatically when the current generation finishes.
  steer: redirect the in-flight generation with the prompt instead of waiting; use it to adjust work that is already running. Falls back to queue when nothing is running.

Important rules for prompt:
  First complete any requested setup, table inspection, analysis, or data changes.
  Do not pass setup, analysis, or data-seeding steps to App Builder.
  Include only the app purpose, UI/workflow, explicit constraints, relevant table IDs, and verified data context.
  Keep the user intent without adding extra features or details.
  Do not use markdown formatting in the prompt.
  Do not specify technology stack unless the user explicitly requests it.

Workflow:
  Use get-apps tool first to check existing apps.
  If a matching app exists, use update action.
  Otherwise, use create action.

commands.help:
Usage: teable app [options] [command]

app operations (list, get-code, create, update, delete, publish, status, unpublish, login-config,
ai-docs, ai-enable, init, clone, pull, push, versions, rollback)

Options:
  -h, --help              display help for command

Commands:
  list [options]          Get all apps in the project
  get-code [options]      Download app source code as a local read-only context snapshot
  create [options]        Create or update an app with AI
  update [options]        Create or update an app with AI
  delete [options]        Delete an app
  publish [options]       Publish an app. Returns success/failed when final; if it returns
                          deploying, poll app status until success/failed
  status [options]        Check app publish status after publish returns deploying
  unpublish [options]     Unpublish an app
  login-config [options]  Configure login/authentication for an app
  ai-docs [options]       How the app calls AI through Teable proxy (usage + available model keys)
  ai-enable [options]     Enable AI access for an app (provisions the AI proxy key)
  init [options]          Create an app and check out its repository locally for development with
                          external tools
  clone [options]         Clone an app repository locally for development with external tools
  pull [options]          Update a local app checkout: fast-forward the repository and refresh
                          instructions, env and table context
  push [options]          Push a local app checkout to Teable and record it as a new app version
  versions [options]      List the saved versions of an app
  rollback [options]      Restore an earlier app version as a new version
  help [command]          display help for command

Examples:
  teable app list
  teable app get-code --app-id appXXXX
  teable app init --name "Inventory" --dir ./inventory     # new app, local checkout
  teable app clone --app-id appXXXX                         # existing app, local checkout
  teable app pull                                           # inside a checkout
  teable app push -m "Add stock count page"                 # inside a checkout
  teable app versions --app-id appXXXX
  teable app rollback --app-id appXXXX --to 3
  teable app publish --app-id appXXXX --wait
  teable app create --prompt "A task tracker with status board"
  teable app update --app-id appXXXX --prompt "Add a dark mode toggle"
  teable app delete --app-id appXXXX
  teable app publish --app-id appXXXX
  teable app status --app-id appXXXX
  teable app unpublish --app-id appXXXX
  teable app login-config --app-id appXXXX --login-config '{"enabled":true,"userTableId":"tblXXX","emailFieldId":"fldXXX","providers":[{"type":"email-otp"}]}'
  teable app ai-docs
  teable app ai-enable --app-id appXXXX

subcommands.name: apply
subcommands.summary: Apply an authority config file: reconcile live state to match it
subcommands.description:
Apply a config file to the authority matrix: create/update roles, members,
default role and admins until the live state matches the file.
ALWAYS preview first: `--dry-run` shows exactly what apply would do —
including pending --prune deletions — and runs the same preflight guards;
plain `authority diff` only compares state and does not model --prune.

Roles that exist on the server but not in the file are KEPT unless --prune
is passed. Keys absent from the file are left unchanged (managed-key rule).
The matrix on/off state is never touched — use `authority enable/disable`.

Apply is not atomic: changes run in order (role creation happens before the
default-role change) and stop at the first API error. Re-running apply is
safe — already-applied changes simply no longer show up as differences.

Config-file shape and the full table-grant reference (deny values, field modes, the "Me" current-user filter token): see `teable authority export --help`.

Personal access token; falls back to TEABLE_TOKEN env var

subcommands.name: enable
subcommands.summary: Enable the authority matrix for a project
subcommands.description:
Enable the authority matrix (advanced permissions) for a project.

Once enabled, every collaborator except the project Owner and the matrix admin
users is governed by it: users in enabled roles get their grants, everyone
else falls back to the default role — or LOSES ACCESS when no default role
is set. The command still proceeds in that case but reports a warning;
when in doubt, set "defaultRole" via the config-file flow (export → edit →
diff → apply) first.

subcommands.name: export
subcommands.summary: Export authority matrix config as a JSON file (--role for one role) — start of every grant edit
subcommands.description:
Export the authority matrix (roles, grants, members, default role, admins)
as one declarative JSON document — the starting point of EVERY permission
config change: export → edit the file → `authority diff` to preview →
`authority apply`.

With --role the file contains just that one role, omits the matrix-level
keys and carries `"scope": "role"`; such a partial file only manages that
role and can never prune, which keeps small edits small and safe.

A role grants access TABLE BY TABLE: a table without a grant is completely
invisible to the role's members. Inside a granted table the ceiling is
platform Editor level — matrix roles can never create/delete tables or
fields, or share views.
Once the matrix is enabled it applies to every collaborator except the project
Owner and the matrix admin users. A user in multiple roles gets the UNION of
their grants (most permissive wins).

Config file shape (managed-key rule: a key ABSENT from the file is left
unchanged by diff/apply; an explicitly empty value ([] / null) is enforced.
A full `export` writes every key; `export --role` writes a partial file that
manages only that role):
  {
    "version": 1,
    "baseId": "bseXXXX",
    "scope": "role",           // written by `export --role`; such a file can never
                               // --prune. Omit for a full-matrix file (partiality
                               // alone does NOT protect against --prune)
    "defaultRole": "<role id or name>" | null,   // fallback for unassigned collaborators
    "admins": ["usrXXXX"],                       // users that bypass the matrix
    "roles": [{
      "id": "aurXXXX",          // from export. An entry WITHOUT an id matches an
                                // existing role by name and only creates a new
                                // role when no live role has that name
      "name": "Sales",
      "description": "...",
      "enabled": true,
      "members": { "users": ["usrXXXX"], "departments": [] },
      "permissions": [<table grants, see below>],
      "nodes": [{"nodeType": "workflow"|"app", "nodeId": "...", "enabled": true}]
    }]
  }
A table grant may carry "enabled": false — stored but not in effect (round-
tripped faithfully by export/apply).
members.departments needs an enterprise organization; resolve department ids
via `teable call-api` on GET /organization/department (find it with
`teable search-api --query department`). User ids: `teable get-collaborators`.
Every top-level key follows the managed-key rule, including "roles" itself: a
hand-written file with only "defaultRole"/"admins" and no "roles" key manages
just those.
The matrix on/off state is NOT part of the file — use `authority enable/disable`.

Table grant JSON shape (array; one entry per table the role may access):
  [{
    "tableId": "tblXXXX",
    "access": "editor" | "commenter" | "viewer",  // capability preset (required)
    "deny": ["record|delete", ...],   // optional: take away actions on top of the preset
    "views": ["viwXXXX", ...],        // optional whitelist; omit = all views, [] = none
    "rowFilter": { ... },             // optional: members only see matching rows
                                      //   (same JSON syntax as view filters)
    "fields": { "fldXXXX": "hidden" | "read-only" | ["record|create", ...] }
                                      // optional per-field restriction
  }]
access presets:
  editor    — full table access: record CRUD + comment + copy, manage views,
              import + export (the matrix ceiling; trim it with deny)
  commenter — read + comment + copy + export; cannot change records or views
  viewer    — read + copy + export only
deny values: view|create, view|delete, view|update, table|import, table|export, field|read, record|create, record|delete, record|read, record|update, record|comment, record|copy, record|archive.
fields: "hidden" = field invisible to members; "read-only" = visible, not
editable; an action array disables exactly those record actions
(record|read / record|update / record|create).
Fields added to the table AFTER a field restriction set was stored stay
inaccessible to the role; grant one explicitly with "fldXXXX": [].
rowFilter syntax: see `teable get-doc --topic view.filter`.
For user fields the dynamic current-user filter value is the literal "Me"
(capital M) — lowercase "me" is a plain string and matches nothing.
A table the role should NOT access is simply omitted from the array — there
is no "none" value.

subcommands.description:

Returns the matrix id, enabledTime (set = enabled), defaultRole (the authority
role id applied to collaborators not assigned to any role) and adminUsers

commands.help:
Usage: teable authority [options] [command]

authority operations (get, export, diff, apply, enable, disable, role-list, role-get, role-delete,
role-duplicate)

Options:
  -h, --help                display help for command

Commands:
  get [options]             Get the authority matrix (advanced permissions) config of a project
  export [options]          Export authority matrix config as a JSON file (--role for one role) —
                            start of every grant edit
  diff [options]            Preview what an edited authority config file would change (dry run)
  apply [options]           Apply an authority config file: reconcile live state to match it
  enable [options]          Enable the authority matrix for a project
  disable [options]         Disable the authority matrix for a project (config is kept)
  role-list [options]       List authority roles with their assigned users/departments
  role-get [options]        Get one authority role: members and per-table grants (intent view; --raw
                            for API form)
  role-delete [options]     Delete an authority role and its permission config
  role-duplicate [options]  Duplicate an authority role (optionally including members)
  help [command]            display help for command

Examples:
  teable authority get -b bseXXXX
  # ALL config changes (roles, grants, members, default role, admins) go
  # export → edit → diff → apply:
  teable authority export -b bseXXXX --file authority.json
  teable authority export -b bseXXXX --role "Sales" --file sales.json   # scoped small edit
  teable authority diff -b bseXXXX --file authority.json
  teable authority apply -b bseXXXX --file authority.json
  teable authority enable -b bseXXXX

subcommands.name: activate
subcommands.summary: Activate(enable draft) or deactivate automation
subcommands.description:
Activate, deactivate, or discard changes to an automation workflow.

🔄 Workflow Lifecycle:
   Edit → Test → Activate → Running -> Edit -> Test -> Activate -> ...
                    ↓
              Deactivate → Paused

⚠️ IMPORTANT - Draft System:
- All edits create a DRAFT version (not immediately effective)
- You MUST call activate to apply draft changes to the running automation

📋 Operations:

1️⃣  activate - Enable automation AND apply all draft changes

2️⃣  deactivate - Disable the automation

3️⃣  discard - Discard draft changes and revert to last active version

⚠️  Risk Considerations:
- Activating in production will start sending real emails/API calls
- Consider using askForConfirmation before activating in production
- Deactivating stops all automated actions immediately

💡 Best Practices:
- Monitor the first few runs after activation

subcommands.name: generate-flowchart
subcommands.summary: Generate flowchart for automation script action node
subcommands.description:
Generate a structured flowchart from script analysis and persist it to the action config.

Guidelines:
- Each node = one logical operation, NOT one line of code. Group sequential API calls, assignments, or transforms into a single step.
- Prefer 5-12 nodes for simple scripts; complex scripts with many branches/loops may need more.
- Keep labels short (3-8 words). Omit node description unless the label alone is ambiguous.
- Label edges only for branches ("Yes", "No", "Error", "Each item"); omit label for default/sequential flow.
- Always include exactly one "start" node and one "end" node.

Example (linear script):
  GOOD: start → "Fetch records" → "Transform data" → "Write results" → end
  BAD:  start → "Declare vars" → "Set headers" → "Call fetch" → "Parse JSON" → "Loop row" → …

Example (branching script):
  start → "Validate input" → condition("Has records?") →[Yes]→ "Process records" → "Save results" → end
                                                        →[No]→ "Log empty warning" → end

Teable API server base URL; falls back to TEABLE_ENDPOINT env var, then saved config
JSON: nodes (id, type, label) + edges (source, target). Types: start|end|step|condition|loop|tryCatch
Indent JSON for human readability
Personal access token; falls back to TEABLE_TOKEN env var
The workflow ID
Target project ID (required, e.g. bseXXXX). Set default: `teable config base-id <id>`.

Usage: teable automation generate-script [options]

Update script action with JavaScript code.

⚠️ Read docs first: get-doc topic="automation.api"
⚠️ For sending emails: get-doc topic="automation.send-email"
⚠️ For AI: get-doc topic="automation.ai"
⚠️ For Slack: get-doc topic="integration.slack"

🔧 Available in script:
- process.env.AUTOMATION_TOKEN - Auth token for API calls
  ⚠️ NEVER use TEABLE_TOKEN — it does NOT exist in automation scripts
- process.env.PUBLIC_ORIGIN - Base URL for API
- input[triggerId] - Trigger data (record, fields, etc.)
- input.integrations["<id>"] - Integration info (id, name, provider)
- output.set(key, value) - Return data for next action

🔗 External Integrations:
1. Call get-user-integrations to get integration IDs
2. Pass integrations array: [{ id: "<integration-id>" }]
3. Read integration doc for token access and API usage patterns

📡 API Calls (use fetch with token):

// Send Email
await fetch(process.env.PUBLIC_ORIGIN + "/api/automation/runtime/email", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.AUTOMATION_TOKEN}`, "Content-Type":
"application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ to: "user@example.com", subject: "Hi", body: "Hello" })
});

// Get Records
await fetch(process.env.PUBLIC_ORIGIN + `/api/table/${tableId}/record`, {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.AUTOMATION_TOKEN}` }
});

// Create Records
await fetch(process.env.PUBLIC_ORIGIN + `/api/table/${tableId}/record`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.AUTOMATION_TOKEN}`, "Content-Type":
"application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ records: [{ fields: { Name: "Test" } }] })
});

// Upsert by unique key (sync/import — never create-then-catch-duplicate)
await fetch(process.env.PUBLIC_ORIGIN + `/api/table/${tableId}/record/upsert`, {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.AUTOMATION_TOKEN}`, "Content-Type":
"application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ fieldKeyType: "id", typecast: true, matchField: "fldXXX", onConflict:
"update", records: [{ fields: { fldKey: "ext-1" } }] })
});

⚠️ Rules: Use built-in fetch(), NEVER node-fetch
⚠️ Sync by a unique key MUST use /api/table/<tableId>/record/upsert, never create records and catch
duplicate errors. matchField must be a single field with unique=true; "ignore" does not update
existing rows; "update" only writes the provided columns.

💡 After writing code, test with test-automation-node

subcommands.name: get
subcommands.summary: Get detailed automation workflow
subcommands.description:
Get detailed information about a specific automation workflow.

Returns complete workflow information:
- Workflow metadata (id, name, description, status)
- Draft status (hasDraft) - whether unpublished changes exist
- Edges: execution flow graph (source→target) showing node execution order and dependencies
- Trigger configuration and output variables
- All action nodes with full config (script code, email body/subject, HTTP url/method/body, record fields, etc.)
- Logic/control nodes: conditions (if/else branches), repeat loops, and structural markers
- Recent execution history

Parameters:
- workflowId: The workflow ID to query (required)
- includeActiveSnapshot: Set true to also get the published action configs for comparison (default: false)

Draft System:
- When hasDraft=true on an active workflow, the running version differs from the draft
- Set includeActiveSnapshot=true to see both versions and compare
- Use activate-automation method="activate" to publish draft changes
- Use activate-automation method="discard" to discard draft changes

Use this before modifying an automation to:
- See current trigger configuration
- Understand all action nodes and their full config
- Check available input variables
- Review recent run status

subcommands.description:
Create or update an automation workflow with its trigger.

⚠️ REQUIRED: Before using this tool, you MUST read documentation first:

   get-doc topic="automation.api" - REST API reference for scripts

🎯 Build an automation:
1. Read docs with get-doc (REQUIRED)
2. Call this tool (new: creates trigger + script action; existing: updates only the trigger)
3. Use generate-script-action with the returned actionId to add code (updates return no actionId — target an existing action or set createScriptAction: true)
4. Test with test-automation-node
5. Activate with activate-automation

📋 Trigger Types:

subcommands.name: test-node
subcommands.summary: Test automation trigger or action node
subcommands.description:
Test a specific node (trigger or action) in an automation workflow.

🧪 Testing is ESSENTIAL for building reliable automations!

📋 How to use:
1. After configuring a trigger, test it to capture sample output
2. After adding an action, test it with the trigger output
3. Review the output to verify it works correctly
4. If test fails, analyze the error and fix the configuration

💡 Tips:
- Test trigger first to get sample data
- Test actions in order (each depends on previous outputs)
- Use recordId to pin a specific row for record-based triggers
- A connectorEvent trigger tests on the event it last saw. With none yet it listens for the next real event (up to 30 minutes) instead of returning output; that event becomes its test result by itself.
- scheduledTime triggers auto-synthesize timestamps (no input needed)
- Review output structure to understand available data for next steps

⚠️  Risk considerations:
- Testing with sideEffect=true WILL execute real actions (send emails, API calls)
- Default sideEffect=false is safe for testing
- For production data, consider using askForConfirmation first

Parameters:
- workflowId: The automation workflow ID
- nodeId: The specific node to test (trigger ID or action ID)
- recordId: Optional record ID for record-based triggers
- sideEffect: Whether to execute with real side effects (default: false)
- withDependency: Whether to test dependency nodes together (default: false)

Returns:
- success: Whether the test succeeded
- output: The output data from the node (use this for subsequent actions)
- error: Error message if test failed

commands.name: call-api
commands.summary: Call any Teable API (axios-style: method, url, params, data)
commands.description:
Call any Teable API with axios-style parameters.

IMPORTANT: Use search-api first to find the correct method and URL path.

Parameters:
  - method (required): HTTP method (e.g., "GET", "POST")
  - url (required): URL path template from search-api (e.g., "/table/{tableId}/record")
  - params: Merged path + query parameters — path params are split based on the API specification
  - data: Request body for POST/PUT/PATCH

Example workflow:
  1. search-api({ query: "duplicate record" })
     → Returns: method: "POST", url: "/table/{tableId}/record/{recordId}/duplicate"
  2. call-api({
       method: "POST",
       url: "/table/{tableId}/record/{recordId}/duplicate",
       params: { tableId: "tblXXX", recordId: "recXXX" }
     })

subcommands.help:
Usage: teable field create [options]

Create a field in a table. Fields are like columns in a spreadsheet.

SMART DEFAULTS:
  - Type inference: omit "type" and it will be inferred from options
  - Auto-sanitization: select choices get auto-assigned colors
  - Name resolution: use table/field NAMES instead of IDs where possible
  - Names require baseId (CLI: --base-id); target fields load on demand, unknown names fail before
creation

TYPE ALIASES: text, long, num, sel, multi, check, rate, date, user, file, link, rollup, formula,
condRollup

BASIC FIELDS: text/long/num/date/check/rate/sel/multi/user/file

LINK - Connect tables
  options: { foreignTableName: "Projects" } or { foreignTableId: "tblXXX" }

LOOKUP - Display data from linked tables
  isLookup: true + lookupOptions: { linkFieldName: "Project", lookupFieldName: "Status" }
  (or use IDs: linkFieldId, lookupFieldId)
  Omit type with baseId to inherit the target field type. Without baseId, provide IDs and an
explicit type.

ROLLUP - Aggregate values from linked records
  lookupOptions: { linkFieldName: "Tasks", lookupFieldName: "Hours" }
  options: { expression: "SUM({values})" }

FORMULA - Calculate values (field names auto-converted to IDs)
  options: { expression: "{Budget} - {Actual}" }

CONDITIONAL LOOKUP - Query ANY table with filters (no link needed)
  isLookup + isConditionalLookup + lookupOptions: { foreignTableName, filter, lookupFieldName }

OUTPUT: { field: "fldXXX:Name:type", hint: "..." }

Options:
  --table-id <tableId>           Table ID to create field in
  --name <name>                  Field name
  --type <fieldType>             Field type:
                                 text/num/sel/multi/check/rate/date/user/file/link/rollup/formula/condRollup.

                                 baseId, supply IDs and an explicit type.

Usage: teable field update [options]

• Dot notation: { updates: { "options.formatting.precision": 2 } }

• Type change: { updates: { type: "number", options: {...} } }

commands.name: get-doc
commands.description:
Get comprehensive documentation for Teable features and configurations.
Use this tool to understand configuration formats before creating or updating resources.
For updating all matching rows or choosing a record update mode, read "record.bulk-update".
Workflow:
1. Identify the category needed (field, view, or record)
2. Query the specific subtopic (e.g., "field.formula" or "field.colors")
3. Use examples from documentation to construct correct configurations

options.description: Teable API server base URL; falls back to TEABLE_ENDPOINT env var, then saved config
Indent JSON for human readability
Personal access token; falls back to TEABLE_TOKEN env var

Documentation topic in format "category.subtopic":

Field Configuration:
- field.basic: Basic fields (text, number, date, checkbox, user, attachment, rating)
- field.select: Select fields (single/multiple select with choices)
- field.link: Link fields (relationships between tables)
- field.formula: Formula fields (computed values with expressions)
- field.lookup: Lookup fields (display values from linked records, includes conditional lookup)
- field.rollup: Rollup fields (aggregate values from linked records, includes conditional rollup)
- field.ai: AI-enhanced fields (extraction, classification, etc.)
- field.formatting: Number and datetime formatting options
- field.show-as: Visual representation options (progress bars, rings, charts, clickable links)
- field.colors: Available color options for fields

View Configuration:
- view.filter: Filter records by conditions
- view.sort: Sort records by field values
- view.group: Group records into collapsible sections
- view.column: Configure visible columns and widths

Record Data:
- record.bulk-update: update-records and delete-records condition vs fixed-ID modes, examples, counts and permission safeguards
- record.value-format: Exact format for field values when creating/updating records without typecasting

Automation:
- automation.trigger: Trigger types and configuration (recordCreated, recordUpdated, recordMatchesConditions, formSubmitted, scheduledTime, buttonClick, webhook)
- automation.send-email: SendEmail action configuration with system or custom SMTP
- automation.api: Teable REST API reference for scripts (records, fields, filters)
- automation.ai: Call AI from a script (prompt, attachments, structured output)

External Integrations (for automation scripts):
- integration.slack: Slack API - send messages, notifications, interact with channels and users

Scrape:
- scrape.guide: Find, price and run third-party data endpoints (social platforms, e-commerce, company and people data, search)

App Builder:
- app.ai: How the app calls AI models through the Teable proxy (env vars, server-side usage, available model keys)

Reference:
- reference.url: Teable resource URL patterns and ID prefixes — parse a pasted link into its resource type and IDs, or generate a link to a table/record/automation/app/dashboard
Target project ID (required, e.g. bseXXXX). Set default: `teable config base-id <id>`.

commands.description:
Import tabular data (CSV/Excel/TSV/inline JSON) into Teable.

Behavior — selected by which target flag is set:

  --table-name <name>               → create new table (fields + types inferred from data)

  # Analyze (no target flag) — returns sheets, columns, attachmentToken
  teable import --file data.xlsx

  # Create new table from a file
  teable import --file data.csv --table-name "Users"

  # Append via stdin — mapping auto-inferred when headers match fields
  echo '[{"Title":"Bug 1"}]' | teable import --table-id tblXXX

  # Explicit mapping when headers do NOT match (keys = field name or fldXXX)
  teable import --file legacy.csv --table-id tblXXX --mappings '{"Title":0,"Budget":2}'

  # Reuse attachmentToken from a prior analyze (pick a specific sheet)
  teable import --attachment-token <t> --table-name "Data" --sheet "Sheet2"

Import a Google spreadsheet (each selected tab becomes a table) into Teable using the native importer. Credential is automatic when Google Sheets is connected in the connectors menu — the connected integration's token is resolved and refreshed server-side. Override with --integration-id <id> or --access-token <token>.

subcommands.name: preview
subcommands.summary: Preview a supported write and expose its canonical effects and blockers
subcommands.description:
Preview a canonical Teable write operation as the authenticated caller without executing it.

Always discover support first with get-operation-preview-capabilities. For every supported destructive or non-obvious write, call this tool with the same operation and operation-specific input that the existing write will receive.

Explain outcome, blockers, warnings, coverage.unknown, unknown measures, and capability limitations to the user. A blocked outcome forbids the write. An incomplete outcome or unresolved product-impact uncertainty requires product confirmation before writing.

Only after the preview has been examined and any required confirmation obtained may you invoke the existing write tool or route. External authorization remains host-owned.

Never infer safety from a low complexity score or level, and never treat an empty effects array as proof that the write has no impact.

Returns the canonical HTTP response unchanged: {ok:true,data} or {ok:false,error}, including stable codes and all blocker, coverage, unknown, effect, and complexity fields.

Adoption counts only identified exported SQL/structured execute endpoint SERVER requests in an explicit environment/service/[start,end) window, never all production requests or users. Missing capture scope makes adoption unavailable.

options.description: Exclusive request start, UTC ISO timestamp
Exact resource deployment environment: ai, cn, staging or local
Restricted effective export policy JSON with provenance SHA-256; absent means unknown
Bounded OTLP/JSON export containing executed base SQL spans
Print the structured report instead of a text summary
Inspect at most this many spans (bounded so an unbounded export cannot hang the CLI)
Exact resource service.name (required with environment/start/end)
Inclusive request start, UTC ISO timestamp

subcommands.help:
Usage: teable query coverage [options]

Summarize a restricted OTLP/JSON export. SQL structural coverage remains separate from adoption.
Adoption counts only identified exported SQL/structured execute endpoint SERVER requests in an
explicit environment/service/[start,end) window, never all production requests or users. Missing
capture scope makes adoption unavailable.

Options:
  --file <path>           Bounded OTLP/JSON export containing executed base SQL spans
  --max-spans <count>     Inspect at most this many spans (bounded so an unbounded export cannot
                          hang the CLI)
  --environment <name>    Exact resource deployment environment: ai, cn, staging or local
  --service <name>        Exact resource service.name (required with environment/start/end)
  --start <utc>           Inclusive request start, UTC ISO timestamp
  --end <utc>             Exclusive request start, UTC ISO timestamp
  --export-policy <path>  Restricted effective export policy JSON with provenance SHA-256; absent
                          means unknown
  --json                  Print the structured report instead of a text summary (default: false)
  -h, --help              display help for command

Input must be a single OTLP/JSON object with resourceSpans[].scopeSpans[].spans[].
Capture the JSON body an SDK/collector sends to /v1/traces (protocol http/json),
or any backend export that preserves OTLP JSON. Other formats are rejected.
Exports larger than 20 MiB are rejected and at most 100000 spans are inspected;
records/aggregate candidates are migration hints, not semantic equivalence.
Counts are exported execution spans, not unique production requests, and one
execution is counted once regardless of how many tables it references.
Adoption requires --environment, --service, --start and --end together.
SDK sampled flags are not an export ratio. No inverse weighting is applied.
Missing parents, environments, timestamps and capped rows remain explicit.
Reports are aggregate-only: no SQL, raw attributes, App/query/user IDs or URLs.

Examples:
  teable query coverage --file traces.json
  teable query coverage --file traces.json --max-spans 20000 --json
  teable query coverage --file traces.json --environment ai --service teable-backend --start 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z --end 2026-11-02T00:00:00Z --json

subcommands.help:
Usage: teable query explain [options]

Explain one inline structured query through the canonical HTTP protocol: admission, schema, binding,
authorization and routing run as the authenticated caller, but the business SELECT is not executed
and no rows are returned. Output includes caller-scoped SQL, ordered parameter names, an explicitly
generic or structural plan summary, and timing. Opt-in only: the selected host must enable
V2_DATA_QUERY_ENABLED or V2_DATA_QUERY_EXECUTE_ENABLED (default false).

Options:
  --request <json|@file>                Canonical request JSON literal or @path/to/request.json
  --table-id <tableId>                  Stable table ID (inline form)
  --select <json|@file>                 JSON array of {fieldId|system|expr,alias} projections
                                        (inline form)
  --filter <json|@file>                 JSON legacy field filter, boolean formula, or filter group
  --relations <json|@file>              JSON map of relation aliases to { linkFieldId, tableId,
                                        filter? }; uses version 2 unless formula projections or
                                        filters require version 3
  --sort <json|@file>                   JSON array of sort expressions
  --parameter-definitions <json|@file>  JSON map of declared parameter types
  --parameters <json|@file>             JSON map of runtime parameter values
  --limit <limit>                       Maximum planned rows (default: 100; max: 1000) (default:
                                        "100")
  --offset <offset>                     Rows to skip (default: 0)
  --record-id <recordId>                Optional controlled record identity
  --query-id <queryId>                  Optional observability name
  --token <token>                       Personal access token; falls back to TEABLE_TOKEN env var
  --endpoint <endpoint>                 Teable API server base URL; falls back to TEABLE_ENDPOINT
                                        env var, then saved config
  --pretty                              Indent JSON for human readability (default: false)
  -h, --help                            display help for command

Use --request alone for the canonical JSON form, or the inline flags without --request.
Formula projections or boolean formula filters infer version 3; legacy flags retain version 1/2 inference.
Use --request @request.json to supply an explicit definition.version, including version 3.
Examples:
  teable query explain --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:3000 --request @request.json
  teable query explain --table-id tblXXX --select '[{"fieldId":"fldXXX","alias":"title"}]' --limit 20
  teable query explain --table-id tblXXX --select @select.json --relations @relations.json
  teable query explain --table-id tblXXX --select '[{"expr":{"type":"formula","formula":"UPPER({title})","references":{"title":{"type":"field","fieldId":"fldXXX"}}},"alias":"title"}]'
  teable query explain --table-id tblXXX --select @select.json --filter '{"type":"formula","formula":"{amount} >= {minimum}","references":{"amount":{"type":"field","fieldId":"fldXXX"},"minimum":{"type":"parameter","name":"minimum"}}}' --parameter-definitions '{"minimum":{"type":"number"}}' --parameters '{"minimum":100}'
Use Teable formula syntax and explicit references; bind runtime values with declared parameters, never text interpolation.
A boolean formula is itself a filter leaf; use conjunction/items or not to combine it with legacy field filters. Standalone operands, comparison nodes and null-test nodes are not supported.
Inline LAST_MODIFIED_TIME({field}) is not supported; reference a stored formula field instead. Zero-argument LAST_MODIFIED_TIME() remains supported.

Stdout is {ok:true,data:{sql,parameters,plan,timing}} or {ok:false,error}.
A protocol failure exits nonzero. Bind values, host permission predicates and rows are never printed.

This is an ephemeral development read. It never writes App files or creates a named query.
Formula projections or boolean formula filters infer version 3; legacy flags retain version 1/2 inference.
For an explicit definition.version (including aggregates), use query execute --request @request.json.
Examples:

Use Teable formula syntax, not SQL. Every {alias} is resolved only through that formula's references.
A boolean formula is itself a filter leaf; combine it with legacy field filters using conjunction/items or not. Standalone operands, comparison nodes and null-test nodes are not supported.

cross-products, authoring-size limits and the SQL retirement freeze. Warnings exit 0 by default;
--strict turns any warning into exit 1. `mode: sql-query` warns (data_query.sql_query_frozen);
`mode: auto` reports its frozen, never-executed fallback as info. This is authoring-time only and
never changes backend save/publish validation.

COMBINATORIAL_MANIFEST, UNUSED_QUERY, data_query.sql_query_frozen (warnings) and
QUERY_USAGE_UNKNOWN, data_query.auto_sql_fallback (info).

subcommands.name: delete
subcommands.summary: Delete matching records by filter or a fixed selection of IDs
subcommands.description:
Delete records by a condition or by a fixed selection of record IDs.

Choose exactly one selector:
  - filter: Nonempty canonical filter with resolved field IDs; deletes matching permitted rows synchronously on the server.
  - recordIds: IDs already read or explicitly selected (max 1000).
For conditions, first get-fields to resolve readable field IDs, then pass filter directly; do not fetch record IDs or use SQL to delete.
Filters support nested and/or conjunctions with items (or filterSet), and not. Empty or malformed filters and unreadable predicate fields are rejected.
A permission or conditional deletion error is a failure; do not retry through ID enumeration or another selector.

Returns success and deletedCount; conditional mode reports actual committed deletions (0 when no rows match).

Examples:
  { tableId: "tblXXX", filter: { fieldId: "fldStatus", operator: "is", value: "Archived" } }
  { tableId: "tblXXX", recordIds: ["rec001", "rec002"] }

subcommands.name: update
subcommands.summary: Update records by condition (filter + fields) or fixed IDs (header + records)
subcommands.description:
Update records in exactly one mode: shared filter+fields or compact header+records.
ROUTING: When the same values apply to all matching records, use filter+fields directly; do not read or enumerate record IDs first. Use header+records for explicit IDs, different values per row, or reordering.
CONDITIONAL FORMAT: {"tableId":"tblXXX","filter":{"fieldId":"fldStatus","operator":"is","value":"Todo"},"fields":{"Status":"Done"},"typecast":true}
Resolve filter field IDs from table metadata. Canonical filters support a condition, {conjunction:"and"|"or",items:[...]}, the filterSet alias, and {not:...}. Empty/malformed filters and empty fields are rejected.
Conditional fields accept names or IDs. null clears; empty string is a value. Returns the actual updatedCount, including 0 for no changes. Unsupported relation/junction updates fail; use records mode with explicit IDs instead.

RECORDS FORMAT:
{
  "tableId": "tblXXX",
  "header": ["recordId", "Name", "Status"],
  "records": [
    ["recAAA", "Updated Name A", "Done"],
    ["recBBB", "Updated Name B", "Pending"]
  ]
}

RULES:
- header: First element MUST be "recordId"
- records: First value in each row is the record ID to update
- Empty string "": Skip field (no change) in records mode only
- null: Clear the cell

VALUE TYPES: Same as create-records

REORDER (records mode only, optional):
  "order": { "viewId": "viwXXX", "anchorId": "recYYY", "position": "before"|"after" }
  Moves record(s) before/after the anchor in the given view.
  Swap rows A↔B: call twice with different anchors.

subcommands.summary: Create a routine triggered by a schedule or a connector event (dry-run to preview, then draft/run/activate)
subcommands.description:
Create a routine: a headless agent task run by a dedicated bot, started either by a schedule ("summarize new feedback rows every morning at 9") or by an event from a connected app (triggerType connectorEvent).

subcommands.name: upsert
subcommands.summary: Record or update a tool so it survives sandbox rebuilds
subcommands.description: Record one tool: its setup command, the $HOME directories holding state that command cannot regenerate, a description — each optional, in any combination. Keyed by name — running this again updates the record in place (paths accumulate); never delete and re-add, which would destroy the state in between. A path belongs to exactly one tool: record a companion sharing the directory with --command only. Existing ~/.<name>, ~/.local/share/<name> and ~/.local/state/<name> dirs are discovered and persisted automatically. Each --path is moved into ~/.teable/home now and symlinked back; after a rebuild the symlinks are restored and `setup <name>` replays the command on demand. Always give a --description: the agent decides from it whether a recorded tool fits a task. Pin versions in the command (e.g. npm i -g <package>@<version>) for reproducible rebuilds. Prefer $KEY references (stored via `teable env set`) over embedding secrets in the command.

subcommands.name: run
subcommands.summary: Get third-party data — social platforms, e-commerce, company and people data, search results — by running an endpoint found with scrape-search
subcommands.description:
Run an endpoint found with `teable scrape search`, its input built from `teable scrape inspect`.
A sync endpoint prints the data; an async one prints its jobId at once while the job keeps running. Fetch that result with `teable scrape status --job-id <id> --wait 60`. Never run this again for the same input: that starts and bills a second run.

Third-party data the plain web cannot give: social platforms (LinkedIn, Instagram, TikTok, X, YouTube, Facebook, Reddit, Douyin, Xiaohongshu, Bilibili...), e-commerce (Amazon, Walmart, eBay...), company and people enrichment, web/news/maps search, SEO, finance and US real-estate data.
When to reach for it: the task needs facts or data from outside the project and the user's own accounts — mining data (leads, companies, people, products, prices, reviews, posts, search results) or verifying a fact that depends on live or platform data (someone's current role, a company's size or funding, a product's price, an account's followers). Search here before inventing sample data, saying the data is unavailable, or writing your own scraper. Not for what you already know reliably — every run is billed.
Not a page reader: an ordinary public web page is fetched directly, for free. When that fetch fails, is blocked, or cannot give the structured data needed, use scrape.
Not a connected app either: an app the user connected (Composio or OAuth) is their own account — their inbox, their posts, their CRM. Public data of a platform (someone's profile by URL, posts by keyword, search results) is a scrape even when the user has that app connected.

Workflow:
1. scrape-search. When the request names a platform (the scraper menu's prompt does, with a "Data type" when the user picked one): platform = its id (youtube, linkedin, company-enrichment...) and type = the data type (profile, posts, videos, comments, channel, company, jobs, search, hashtag, followers, products, reviews, ads, transcript, music, places, news, events, shop). That lists every source for that kind of data on that platform, each with its requiredInputs: pick the one whose required inputs are what the user gave (url for a link; query, name or keyword for words), and of those that fit equally, the cheaper. Otherwise query = platform and data type ("linkedin person profile"), useCase = the user's request in their words.
2. scrape-inspect only the one you will run: read inputSchema and, when present, outputSchema (the fields a run returns). Inspect a second only if the first cannot take the input. Never guess input fields.
3. scrape with that endpoint and an input matching the schema. One run reads one input (one URL, one keyword...); run again per item.
The scraper menu's prompt names a platform, maybe a "Data type", and ends with "What to scrape: …" — that is the input, never a table name: a link is the page or object to read, a bare word or phrase is a keyword search on that platform; a company name with Profile means its company page, a person's name their profile or a people search. Run with it; do not ask the user to restate what they typed, and never ask to confirm a single run.
A request that names a source ("use Bright Data") pins that source; one that names an endpoint id skips the search: inspect and run that endpoint. When adding to a table earlier runs filled, reuse their endpoint so the columns line up.

Say which source the data came from; do not report prices or credits — the transcript shows what each run cost. A run over the per-run limit is refused by the server: pick a cheaper endpoint or a smaller input, or say why neither works.
Keep volume fields (limit, count, max_results...) small unless the user asks for more; an endpoint without a limit field returns as many results as it finds.
A run is billed whatever the outcome, so never re-run the same input to retry a pending job: resume it with scrape-status.

commands.summary: Search available APIs by description to find the right endpoint
commands.description:
Search available Teable APIs by keyword or description.

Returns APIs matching your permission level. Use with call-api to execute.

Parameters:
  - query (required): Search keywords in any language
  - tags: Filter by API category (e.g., ["record", "field"])
  - limit: Max results (default: 5, max: 10)

Returns API details including:
  - method, url: Pass directly to call-api
  - summary, description
  - parameters: Required and optional params with descriptions
  - requestBody: Body schema for POST/PUT/PATCH endpoints

Example: search-api({ query: "update records" })
  → { method: "PATCH", url: "/table/{tableId}/record", parameters: [...], requestBody: {...} }
  → call-api({ method: "PATCH", url: "/table/{tableId}/record", params: { tableId: "tblXXX" }, data: { ... } })

commands.name: sql-query
commands.description:
⚠️ READ-ONLY SQL Query Tool - Only SELECT statements allowed. No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL.

Execute PostgreSQL 15.4 queries and return results.

## CRITICAL: Use Database Names, NOT Display Names or IDs

Before executing SQL, you MUST:
1. get dbTableName (NOT the table's display name)
2. get dbFieldName for each field (NOT the field ID like fldXXX)

## SQL Generation Rules

### Table Reference
- Table format: "baseId"."dbTableName" (e.g., "bseXXX"."receipts")
- ❌ WRONG: "bseXXX"."Receipts" (display name)
- ✅ CORRECT: "bseXXX"."receipts" (dbTableName)

### Column Reference  
- Use dbFieldName from get-fields (e.g., "vendor_name", "total_amount")
- ❌ WRONG: "fld1Y0f3b2ryDV9N2MR" (field ID)
- ✅ CORRECT: "vendor_name" (dbFieldName)

### System Fields (always available)
- "__id" - Record ID (text)
- "__auto_number" - Auto-increment number (int)
- "__created_time" - Creation timestamp (timestamptz, UTC)
- "__last_modified_time" - Last modified timestamp (timestamptz, UTC, nullable)
- "__created_by" - Creator user ID (varchar)
- "__last_modified_by" - Last modifier user ID (varchar, nullable)
- "__version" - Record version (int)

### Identifiers & Syntax
- Use double quotes for ALL identifiers: SELECT "field" FROM "schema"."table"

### Result Limits
- Non-aggregate queries: Always add LIMIT 100
- Aggregate/statistical queries: No limit required

### Data Type Handling
- **Numbers**: Use CAST(COUNT(*) AS text) for aggregates to avoid overflow
- **Dates**: Database stores UTC. Convert timezone: timezone('Asia/Shanghai', date_column)
  Format with: to_char(timezone('TZ', col), 'YYYY-MM-DD HH24:MI:SS')
- **JSON fields**: Use json_extract_path_text("field"::json, 'key') to extract values

## Parameters
- sql: The SELECT query using dbTableName and dbFieldName

subcommands.help:
Usage: teable template guide-save [options]

Saves the guide people get after installing this project as a template: a card in their project
whose steps tick themselves from the data. The file replaces the whole draft (read the current one
with `teable template guide` first); it ships with the next `teable template submit`. Read the
guide-writing rules below before writing one.

Options:
  --file <path>           JSON file with the whole guide
  --clear                 Remove the guide: the next submission goes without one
  -b, --base-id <baseId>  Target project ID (required, e.g. bseXXXX). Set default: `teable config
                          base-id <id>`.
  --token <token>         Personal access token; falls back to TEABLE_TOKEN env var
  --endpoint <endpoint>   Teable API server base URL; falls back to TEABLE_ENDPOINT env var, then
                          saved config
  --pretty                Indent JSON for human readability (default: false)
  -h, --help              display help for command

Guide file (JSON, ids from this project):
  {"version": 1, "business"?: {"tableId", "fieldId"}, "steps": [step, ...], "daily"?: [{"workflowId", "text"}]}
  step: {"id", "title", "line", "open": {"type", "id", "target"?}, "done": {"kind", ...}}
  open.type: table | app | workflow | dashboard
  business: the table and field holding the business name; only a renamed step needs it.
  daily: at most 2, 40 chars each; what keeps running once every step is done.

Writing it:
- 3-6 steps, in the order a new user sets things up. id: a short slug (letters, digits, - _),
  kept across edits.
- title: an action, at most 40 chars ("Add your first client"). line: one sentence, at most
  80 chars: what to do and why. Plain words: no ids, field types or jargon.
- done: what the data can prove. Prefer, in this order:
    renamed: the business name no longer holds the sample one
    changed {tableId, fieldId}: a value other than the shipped ones appears in the field
    real {tableId, fieldId, linkFieldId?}: a record whose email in fieldId is not on
      example.com (and whose linkFieldId is filled)
    cleared {tableId, fieldId}: no example.com email is left in the field
    appPublished {appId}: the app is published
    automationSucceeded {workflowId}: the automation has run successfully once
    connected: every account the template asks for is connected
    manual: the user ticks it. Only when nothing above fits.
- open.target: on a table step, {"fieldId"} of the column to fill. On an app step,
  {"anchor"} only when the app has an element marked data-guide="<anchor>" (search its code).
- Leave out business.sample and the samples of changed: they are read from the records on
  submit.
- real and cleared tell sample people from real ones by email: sample emails must be on
  example.com.
- If the project has a Playbook app, or an app with lib/playbook.ts describing setup steps,
  take the steps from it.

Result: `alreadyTrue` lists steps the data, as it would ship, already satisfies. They would
start ticked and submitting refuses them: change their done condition (or the sample data)
and save again. `problem` says why the guide could not be checked.

commands.name: trigger-ai-fill
commands.summary: Trigger AI generation for an AI-configured field
commands.description:
Trigger AI generation for an AI-configured field.

IMPORTANT: Creating/updating a field with aiConfig does NOT automatically generate content.
You MUST call this tool after setting up an AI field to actually run the AI generation.

MODES:
  - Single cell: provide recordId to fill one specific record
  - Batch fill: omit recordId to fill multiple records

OPTIONS:
  - mode: "all" (default) overwrites existing values
  - mode: "emptyOnly" only fills cells that are currently empty
  - viewId: limit to records visible in a specific view

EXAMPLES:
  1. Fill all records: { tableId, fieldId }
  2. Fill one record: { tableId, fieldId, recordId: "recXXX" }
  3. Fill empty only: { tableId, fieldId, mode: "emptyOnly" }

Returns taskId for background processing. AI generation runs asynchronously.
Success means the background task was accepted, not that generated values are ready.

commands.help:
Usage: teable view [options] [command]

view operations (create, get, update, delete)

Options:
  -h, --help        display help for command

Commands:
  create [options]  Create a new view in a table
  get [options]     Get all views in a table
  update [options]  Update view configuration
  delete [options]  Delete a view permanently
  help [command]    display help for command

Examples:
  teable view get --table-id tblXXXX
  teable view create --table-id tblXXXX --name "My Grid" --type grid
